data.title: Suspicious "final demand before seizure" from EuroClaim (€287.40)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 for an alleged phone-concluded prize-draw subscription, payable by 6 August 2026 to a Lithuanian account held by a private person. It shows several scam indicators.
data.explanation: This letter demands €287.40 within 72 hours and threatens account seizure, a negative SCHUFA entry and criminal charges. These are pressure tactics. A real debt collector must name the original creditor clearly, itemise the claim, and cannot seize accounts without a court order. The payment goes to a foreign IBAN held by a private individual, which is a strong warning sign. Do not pay yet. If you never signed up, dispute the claim in writing and ask for proof of the contract. Consider contacting a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police. Do not call the numbers in the letter.

warnings: Payee IBAN is Lithuanian and the account holder is a private person, not the collection company.
Extreme 72-hour pressure and threats of seizure, SCHUFA entry and criminal complaint without a court order are typical scam patterns.
Generic salutation 'Sehr geehrte/r Schuldner/in' and vague extra fees (€24 account fee) are suspicious.
The claim that objection is 'zwecklos' is false; you may dispute an unfounded claim.
